capture.final_message:
Use categorical duality throughout.

- A \(J\)-shaped colimit in \(C\) is exactly a \(J^{\mathrm{op}}\)-shaped limit in \(C^{\mathrm{op}}\). Applying this correspondence to `F.rightOp`, whose opposite-side functor is `F`, turns reflection of \(J^{\mathrm{op}}\)-limits by \(F\) into reflection of \(J\)-colimits by `F.rightOp`.

- Likewise, for \(K : J \to C\), a colimit cocone on \(K\) becomes a limit cone on `K.op`. The image of this cone under `F.op` is the opposite of the cocone obtained by applying \(F\). Hence preservation of the limit of `K.op` by `F.op` transports back to preservation of the colimit of \(K\) by \(F\).

Organize the result by splitting the conjunction and, in each component, applying the existing limits/colimits-under-opposite API. The only essential bookkeeping is that passing to opposites reverses both morphisms and variance, explaining the use of `Jᵒᵖ`, `K.op`, `F.op`, and `F.rightOp`.
